'''Tahir Hussain''' (1923– 21 December 2010) was a Pakistani [[Nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] and an [[emeritus professor]] of physics at the [[Government College University, Lahore|Government College University]] whose research focused on understanding the [[Linear particle accelerator|particle accelerator]].<ref name="Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust" />

==Biography==

Hussain was born in 1923 in [[Aligarh]], [[Uttar Pradesh]] in the [[British Indian Empire]].<ref name="Dawn Newspaper, 2010">{{cite news |last1=Newspaper |first1=the |title=Nuclear physicist Dr Husain dies |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/592535 |accessdate=28 April 2020 |work=DAWN.COM |agency=Dawn |publisher=Dawn Newspaper |date=21 December 2010 |location=Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan |language=en-us }}</ref> He did his graduation in physics from the [[Aligarh Muslim University]] (AMU), and earned [[Master of Science|MSc]] in physics with honours.<ref name="Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust">{{cite web |title=Dr. Tahir Hussain |url=http://nazariapak.info/Famous-Pakistani/Scientists.php |website=nazariapak.info |publisher=Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust |accessdate=28 April 2020}}</ref> At the invitation of the Governor-General of Pakistan [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah]] in 1948, he emigrated to Pakistan along with Dr. [[Rafi Muhammad Chaudhry|R.M. Chaudhry]], accepting a teaching position as laboratory lecturer at the [[Government College, Lahore|Government College University]] in Lahore at the behest of  [[Rafi Muhammad Chaudhry|R.M. Chaudhry]].{{rp|19;69}}<ref name="Comsat, Hussain">{{cite web |last1=Hussain, PhD |first1=Tahir |title=Physics Education in Pakistan: An Account of the Early Decades |url=http://comsats.org/Publications/Books_SnT_Series/08.%20Physics%20in%20Developing%20Countries%20-%20Past,%20Present%20and%20Future%20(April%202006).pdf |website=www.comsats.org |publisher=COMSATS |accessdate=28 April 2020 |location=Islamabad, Pakistan |pages=227 |language=en-us |date=12 April 2006 }}</ref>

On a scholarship, Hussain went to the United Kingdom to attend [[Oxford University]] where he was conferred with a [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] in Nuclear physics in 1954.<ref name="Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust" /><ref name="Dawn Newspaper, 2010" /><ref name="Vallancey Press">{{cite book |title=Who's who in Atoms |date=1969 |publisher=Vallancey Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bdfaAAAAMAAJ&q=husain |language=en}}</ref> Upon returning, he taught courses on [[solid-state physics]] in 1955, and took over the chairmanship of the department of physics at the Government College University in 1962.{{rp|38;70}}<ref name="Comsat, Hussain"/> In 1955, he founded the Center For Advance Studies in Physics (CASP), and served as its founding director.<ref>.{{Cite web
  | last =
  | first =
  | authorlink =
  | author2 =
  | title =Center For Advance Studies in Physics (CASP)
  | website =Government College University press
  | publisher =Chief Librarian GC University Library
  | year =2001
  | url =http://www.gcu.edu.pk/casp.htm
  | doi =
  | accessdate =28 Apr 2010
  | archive-date =7 March 2020
  | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20200307052735/http://www.gcu.edu.pk/CASP.htm
  | url-status =dead
  }}</ref>

In the 1950s–60s, he visited the United States as a post-doctoral fellow at the [[State University of New York]], [[University of Chicago]], and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT),  as well as visiting [[Harvard University]] and [[Stanford University]] in California.<ref name="Comsat, Hussain"/> He also visited [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]], and upon returning, he established the Nuclear Research Laboratory in Lahore based on Lawrence Livermore while updating the teaching program in physics at his university.{{rp|74}}<ref name="Comsat, Hussain"/>

In 1965–69, he was appointed as [[Vice-Chancellor]] of the [[University of Azad Jammu and Kashmir|University of Azad Kashmir]], and later found employment with the [[Ministry of Education (Pakistan)|Pakistani Ministry of Education]] as a consultant on education. He chaired the [[EducationUSA]] network in Pakistan through the Ministry of Education.<ref name="Nazaria-i-Pakistan Trust" />

In 1972, Hussain was delegated to provide consultation on the studies of [[mass–energy equivalence]] and [[radioactive decay]] by the Nuclear Physics Group studying under Dr.  [[Ishfaq Ahmad]], who was secretly working on the [[Pakistan and weapons of mass destruction|nuclear weapons program]].<ref>{{Citation
  | last = Rehman
  | first = Shahid-Ur-
  | author-link = Shahid-Ur-Rehman
  | title = The Nuclear Physics Group at PAEC
  | journal =
  | volume =
  | pages =
  | date = October 1972
  }}
</ref>

Throughout his career, Hussain remained on the teaching faculty at the Government College University, and wrote a college physics book, ''Fundamentals of Physics'' in 1970, which has been published in new editions since.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fundamentals of physics |url=http://nkcs.org.np/cdc/library/opac_css/index.php?lvl=notice_display&id=899 |accessdate=28 April 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Tahir Hussain died on 21 December 2010 aged 87. A condolence reference for Hussain, was organized in Government College University in Lahore.<ref>{{cite news |title=Condolence |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/archive/print/276893-briefs... |accessdate=28 April 2020 |work=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en}}</ref>
